title: Compatibility with finite scalar extension
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E\subset E'$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the completed integral coefficient categories and their raw rationalizations $\Dbc(T,E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], with no Karoubi envelope. Derived scalar extension means integral change of completed coefficient rings followed by scalar localization. Then it defines an exact functor
$$T_{E'/E}=E'\otimes_E^L-:\Dbc(T,E)\longrightarrow\Dbc(T,E').$$
Choose $T_{E/E}=\operatorname{id}$ literally. For $E\subset E'\subset E''$, balancing of derived tensor specifies an exact natural isomorphism
$$a_{E'',E',E}:T_{E''/E'}T_{E'/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{E''/E}.$$
The associators satisfy the unit equations and the pentagon for four nested fields. There are canonical natural shift comparisons
$$\sigma_{E'/E,K}:T_{E'/E}(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(T_{E'/E}K)[1]$$
commuting with these associators.

Write $C_{E'/E,T}(K)=K\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E',T}$ for the integral ambient scalar-extension functor; its constructible restriction and rationalization is $T_{E'/E,T}$. For morphisms $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ between schemes satisfying the same scheme hypotheses, there are coherent comparisons on ambient derived-complete integral categories
$$C_{E'/E,Y}Rf_{*,\mathcal O_E}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,\mathcal O_{E'}}C_{E'/E,X},\qquad
C_{E'/E,Y'}Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp},\mathcal O_E}\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp},\mathcal O_{E'}}C_{E'/E,Y}.$$
Their restrictions and rationalizations are comparisons on $\Dbc$ whenever the displayed operations preserve those constructible categories; no preservation assertion for arbitrary $f$ is implicit. Here ordinary direct image is the ringed-topos derived direct image, and completed pullback is [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. For a cartesian square $(f,f',g,g')$ whose four schemes satisfy the stated hypotheses, the exchange is the canonical ambient ringed-topos mate of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], followed by derived completion and the direct-image/completion comparison, and then rationalization. Under the displayed comparisons, scalar extension of this $E$-exchange is this $E'$-exchange. The comparisons respect identity morphisms, composition, successive coefficient extensions and shifts.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E,B=\mathcal O_{E'},t=\varpi_E,v=\varpi_{E'}$. The DVR factorization gives $t=wv^e$ with $w\in B^\times$, $e\geq1$, and finite residue fields. The finite-free completed comparison makes $S_T$ a finite free $R_T$-module of rank $[E':E]$.

proof.text: The constructible scalar-transport lemma puts $K\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$ in the integral constructible category over $B$ for every integral constructible $K$ over $A$, with the same strata and local models $S_T\otimes_B^L(B\otimes_AP)$. Ambient change of rings is exact and both integral categories carry the inherited triangles, so ambient tensor restricts to an exact integral functor.

proof.text: Use normalized derived tensor units and associators; K-flat scalar change computes successive tensors. Both pentagon routes send $(((p\otimes s)\otimes u)\otimes z)$ to $p\otimes suz$; unit routes multiply by one. Normalize repeated fields literally to identity. For shift compatibility, identify the chosen scalar adjunction with the adjunction normalized by its unit on K-flat resolutions. The normalized-unit right Kan argument makes this adjunction commute with shifts. Exact derived restriction composition commutes with shifts, hence its inverse adjunction conjugate, the actual ambient associator, does too. The faithful full integral inclusion and scalar localization, which is surjective on objects, detect this equation. Conjugation by the specified normalization isomorphisms gives the stated literal-stage associator shift equation.

proof.text: Tensor is semilinear: $C(af)=aC(f)$. Since $t=wv^e$ is invertible after inverting $v$, semilinear localization gives the exact raw rational functor and preserves these coherence equations.

proof.text: Using coefficient inverse image on each edge, let $\beta_f$ be the counit-tensor mate of the finite-free direct-image lemma. It is invertible in $D(S)$ and respects shifts and coefficient towers. Pushforward preserves completeness by the ringed completion theorem; the constant-completion equivalence identifies the PBC convention.

proof.text: Apply strict-tower tensor transport to augmented Koszul towers, including connecting maps and units. Completion transport gives the unit-normalized $\kappa:C\Lambda_R\cong\Lambda_SC$. Ringed monoidal composition and the K-flat scalar-comparison theorem give the invertible ordinary balancing $Lg_S^*C\cong CLg_R^*$ and its composition law; the balancing-coherence theorem normalizes its towers. Follow it by $\kappa^{-1}$ for the completed pull square. For shift compatibility of the actual comparisons, first prove the ordinary derived scalar/pullback comparison commutes with shifts by its counit normalization on flat-term K-flat resolutions. Resolve arbitrary complexes and use density to detect the shift equation. The normalized-unit right Kan argument makes the actual derived pull/push adjunction commute with shifts, so taking its mate proves the direct-image shift equation. The scalar completion comparison commutes with shifts because its unit-normalization equation does, and completion units detect arrows into complete objects. Pasting these shift-compatible maps proves the completed-pull shift equation.

proof.text: Ringed monoidal composition and the composition law $\theta_{gf}=(f^*\theta_g)(\theta_fg^*)$ of the K-flat scalar comparison give the ordinary pull cube and composition laws; mate pasting gives push composition and identities. The reflected-adjunction-square theorem, with the completed adjunctions and unit-normalized $\kappa$, carries these equations to completed pullback and preserves shifts and coefficient towers. In particular, for completed pullback composition, precompose with the two ordinary-to-completed pullback units. Naturality, scalar unit normalization and ordinary pullback composition identify both resulting arrows. The universal property of completion, transported through the specified completed composition isomorphism, cancels these units and proves the completed composition equation.

blueprint_update.statement:
For a finite extension $E\subset E'$, derived scalar extension is an exact
functor
$$
 T_{E'/E}=E'\otimes_E^L-:
 \Dbc(T,E)\longrightarrow\Dbc(T,E').
$$
Choose $T_{E/E}=\operatorname{id}$ literally. For $E\subset E'\subset E''$,
derived tensor associativity gives a specified exact natural isomorphism
$$
 a_{E'',E',E}:T_{E''/E'}T_{E'/E}
 \xrightarrow{\sim}T_{E''/E}.
$$
These associators satisfy the unit equations and the pentagon for four
nested fields. Exactness supplies natural shift comparisons
$$
 \sigma_{E'/E,K}:T_{E'/E}(K[1])
 \xrightarrow{\sim}(T_{E'/E}K)[1]
$$
which commute with the associators.

There are coherent natural isomorphisms
$$
 E'\otimes_E^LRf_{*,E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}
 Rf_{*,E'}(E'\otimes_E^LK)
$$
and analogous isomorphisms for pullback. Under these isomorphisms, scalar
extension of the $E$-exchange map is the $E'$-exchange map.
